Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

my pronoun

also mine, it’s mine, my dear

classical

Hor. Ep. 1.16.35: pōne, meum est
Ter. Ad. 901: pater mī

meus, mea, meum

pronoun (possessive), first and second declension; vocative masculine mī

my, mine

Agrees with the thing owned, not with the owner. “Mine” is the same word used as a predicate: meum est, it’s mine. Latin leaves the possessive out where the owner is plain from the context (see your); put it in for stress or contrast, and before its noun for weight. In address, mī pater, mea Tullia. For “my own” see own.

Examples

  • pōne, meum est

    Put it down, it’s mine.Hor. Ep. 1.16.35

  • quae tua sunt, tibi habē: quae mea, redde mihi

    What is yours, keep for yourself; what is mine, give back to me.Mart. 10.51.16

  • ‘omnia’ inquit ‘bona mea mēcum sunt’

    “All my goods,” he says, “are with me.”Sen. Ep. 9.18

  • Quid agitur, Aeschine? — Ehem, pater mī, tū hīc erās?

    How are you, Aeschinus? — Oh, my father, you were here?Ter. Ad. 901

  • ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē

    There my little Tullia was waiting for me, on her very birthday.Cic. Att. 4.1.4

  • cūr ego tēcum nōn sum? cūr ocellōs Ītaliae, vīllulās meās, nōn videō?

    Why am I not with you? Why can’t I see my little country houses, the eyes of Italy?Cic. Att. 16.6.2

See also I, your, our, own.
